changes_from_live: zip \d{6} -> \d{6}|[A-Z]\d{2}[A-Z]\d[A-Z]\d. Kazpost introduced 7-character building-level postcodes (A99A9A9, e.g. R00H5A9) and asked foreign posts to use them (USPS IMM revision effective 15 Jun 2023). UPU lists both 999999 and A99A9A9. The old 6-digit codes are still in parallel use, so both must validate.
layout %Z%n%S%n%C%n%A%n%O%n%N -> %N%n%O%n%A%n%Z, %C%n%D%n%S per UPU kazEn.pdf (07/2025): 'postcode, locality' after the street, and raion + oblast only on rural mail.
final.notes: Per USPS, the new codes cover 22 localities so far, so many places only have 6-digit codes. %D carries the raion (sub-province) and %S the oblast; both lines are empty for cities (ASTANA, ATYRAU samples). Caveat: in libaddressinput %D normally means a unit below the city, while a raion sits above the village; if downstream code depends on that meaning, move the raion to dropped_tokens instead. The UPU glossary swaps oblast/raion; the examples label ALMATINSKIY OBLAST as province.

decisions.layout: accepted checker: %N%n%O%n%A%n%Z, %C%n%D%n%S. UPU kazEn.pdf (07/2025) shows 'Z00Y5M7, g. ASTANA' and '010013, g. Astana' after the street, and 'L16T0H2, selo Abay / Karasayskiy raion / ALMATINSKIY OBLAST' for rural mail. The proposed reversed order appears nowhere on the sheet.

decisions.required: kept original: AC. UPU namEn.pdf (09/2018, submitted by NamPost) has an explicit rule: 'If the postcode is not specified in the address, then the town should be included in the line used for the postcode.' So an address without a code is still deliverable. The NamPost list's 'Help improve mail delivery service, always use a Post Code' is advice, not a mandate, and does not override the explicit fallback. The GAI 'require postal codes' list (Aug 2026) is introduced in the same document as the list of countries 'with a postcode system', so it was treated as weak evidence for mandatory Z; the country sheet decided.
